title: [YouPass Collect] - Residential water use in 1988 vs 2008
prompt: The charts below show the residential water use in 1988 and 2008. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The pie charts illustrate the proportion of residential water consumption across five different household activities in 1988 and 2008.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, while water usage for kitchen and bathroom purposes increased over the 20-year period, the opposite trend was observed for the remaining three categories. Additionally, the kitchen became the largest water-consuming area by 2008, whereas garden use, which was substantial in 1988, experienced the sharpest decline to become the smallest category.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Regarding the areas that experienced growth, in 1988, kitchen water use stood at a modest 15%, making it the smallest category, while bathroom usage accounted for a considerably higher proportion at 22%. Over the following two decades, the kitchen saw a dramatic surge of 14 percentage points to reach 29% in 2008, thereby becoming the most significant area of household water consumption. Similarly, bathroom usage also rose steadily, though at a more moderate pace, increasing by 6 percentage points to finish at 28% by the end of the period.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: As for the declining categories, washing machines consumed the largest share of water in 1988 at 25%, followed by garden at 20% and toilet use at 18%. However, garden watering experienced by far the most substantial decrease, plummeting by 13 percentage points to just 7% by 2008, making it the lowest water-consuming activity. Meanwhile, both washing and toilet usage saw more modest declines of 3 and 4 percentage points respectively, falling to 22% and 14% by the final year.
